title: Program Assistant, Artificial Intelligence
gist: A Lawfare job posting for a program assistant to support its AI Research Program, revealing the program's structure: six research domains, a Scaling Laws podcast, a visiting fellows program, invite-only workshops, legislative briefings, and roughly ten commissioned papers per year, positioned as a nonpartisan AI policy shop.

insights.claim: Lawfare's AI Research Program spans six research domains: AI governance and regulation; AI and national security; AI and the economy; AI and the legal system; AI and democratic institutions; and AI safety and catastrophic risk.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Maps the six thematic lanes of a nonpartisan AI policy shop—useful for tracking where influential AI-governance commentary originates.
insights.quote: bridges technical, legal, and policy expertise to inform AI governance across six research domains: AI governance and regulation; AI and national security; AI and the economy; AI and the legal system; AI and democratic institutions; and AI safety and catastrophic risk.

insights.claim: The program's activities include the Scaling Laws podcast, a visiting fellows program with rotating six-month fellowships (one new fellow every three months, two in residence at a time), invite-only workshops, and legislative briefings including nonpartisan AI primers for federal and state legislators.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Shows the channels through which the program reaches lawmakers—directly briefing federal and state legislators on AI is a policy-influence vector.
insights.quote: coordinating logistics across the Scaling Laws podcast, the visiting fellows program, invite-only workshops, and legislative briefings and trainings.

insights.claim: The program runs three to four invite-only workshops per year of 15-20 participants under Chatham House rule, rotating among Washington D.C., San Francisco, Austin, and Minneapolis, and produces roughly ten commissioned papers per year.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: Quantifies the program's convening and output cadence and its geographic footprint across AI policy and tech hubs.
insights.quote: three to four invite-only workshops per year (15–20 participants under the Chatham House rule), held on a rotating basis in Washington, D.C., San Francisco, Austin, and Minneapolis

insights.claim: The role is remote-anchored to Washington D.C. with a salary range of $48,800-$60,000, fully paid health and dental premiums, and a 401(k) with up to 4% employer match.
insights.speaker: Lawfare Blog
insights.so_what: A concrete compensation datapoint for entry-level nonprofit AI-policy roles.
insights.quote: Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience within a range of $48,800–$60,000.
